[00:00] Sofia: okay good afternoon everyone, um 13:27 here. I think we have around 45 minutes so we'll run through the agenda quick, SSO first, then SOC2, then badges, then anything else.
[00:22] Michael: yeah, that works. I'm just flagging budget q2, we need numbers for Okta renewal and the endpoint protection license refresh so that procurement can put in the PO.
[00:45] Priya: noted. On SOC2, I've started the evidence map but need folks to claim owners, some items still missing, like rotate keys for dev infra and access review notes.
[01:10] Jamal: we got the floor plan for the new wing, badge readers shipping next week, we just need the list of employees and contractors who'll be moved. There might be a delay on the electricians but looks okay.
[01:35] Sofia: perfect. On SSO, timeline reminder: Okta contract renewal in May, we wanted to do a consolidation + SSO hardening before then. Michael, can you confirm if budget can be shifted to cover expedited migration if needed?
[01:55] Michael: quick answer, maybe; I need concrete numbers. If the SE, like the SSO consultant cost + Okta enterprise tier bumps are brought to me, we can look at a one-time transfer. But no promises.
[02:20] Priya: also, MFA enforcement windows — we need coms plan. I can draft the security comms but HR needs to help with timing so it's not during new hire week. Evan?
[02:42] Evan: yes, I can coordinate, I'll update the onboarding doc. Also note we still have a few contractors without badges in the system, I'll send the list after the call.
[03:05] Sofia: thanks. I put up a rough cutover runbook in the meeting notes, it's very rough, I might've misspelled some things (Okta transcribed as "Oktae" in the doc, ignore that). The runbook includes a rollback plan, smoke tests, and a stakeholder notification matrix.
[03:35] Speaker 1: um, question about legacy apps — does anyone have an exhaustive list? I know we have several apps still relying on SAML 1.1 and older integrations.
[03:58] Priya: we do, but it's scattered. I'll pull a list from the SSO portal and mark owners, expect it by end of day Friday. There may be some funky service accounts that need special handling.
[04:20] Michael: on the finance side, procurement needs the invoice schedule. Do you have renewal dates for all Okta addons?
[04:45] Sofia: Okta Add-Ons: adaptive MFA, lifecycle management; renewal in May but addons billed monthly — I'll pull exact SKU and billing cadence.
[05:10] Jamal: on physical security, badge readers — are we changing any access groups? New wing will be restricted to engineering and operations for now. We'll need to update RBAC on the readers.
[05:35] Priya: yes update RBAC, and ensure audit logs from the readers are shipped to the SIEM — I noticed the last two days some logs weren't forwarded, maybe a config on the collector.
[06:00] Sofia: that's important. Which collector? is it the new log-shipper we deployed last month?
[06:18] Priya: yeah that one, the Fluent something, might show up as fluint in the transcript, lol. We should iterate the config. I'll raise a ticket.
[06:35] Michael: small ask — can we confirm whether the Okta renewal will be capex or opex? It changes how we account for the expense. CFO prefers capex for multi-year contracts.
[06:55] Sofia: good point. I'll include term options in the cost summary.
[07:10] Evan: related HR: onboarding checklist needs to call out laptop imaging and MFA setup before first day. Can IT provide an imaging window?
[07:33] Sofia: yes, we have imaging slots Mon/Wed/Fri; I'll make sure IT schedulings are on the shared calendar.
[07:55] Jamal: quick note: badge provisioning for the new wing might need temporary guest badges if the electrician access is delayed. That will increase admin overhead.
[08:15] Priya: please ensure temporary badge issuance is logged — we can't have untracked access. Also, let's ensure temporary creds are timeboxed.
[08:35] Sofia: agreed. On backups, we ran the incremental tests last week — restore times look fine for non-prod, but prod full restore hasn't been tested in a while. We should schedule a restore drill.
[08:55] Michael: restore drill could impact billing if we spin up a bunch of instances — need a cost estimate.
[09:15] Sofia: understood, I'll produce a cost estimate for the restore drill and two schedule options.
[09:35] Priya: SOC2: timeline — audit firm wants to start evidence collection mid-April. We need owners to have evidence uploaded two weeks before. I'm aiming to have the map done by 2026-03-18 and assign owners.
[09:58] Michael: what's on the critical list for SOC2? backups, access reviews, encryption config, incident response runbooks?
[10:20] Priya: yep, and vendor attestation for Okta and our endpoint protection provider, plus key management evidence (KMS rotation logs). Some transcripts earlier had KV cache spelled like KV cash, minor typo.
[10:45] Sofia: for KMS, we moved to a new key policy last quarter, need to ensure rotation events are in the logs — I'll pull the rotation window.
[11:05] Jamal: any procurement blockers on badge readers? We've pre-approved the vendor but shipping ETA could slip.
[11:25] Michael: procurement to confirm if vendor invoice needs PO up front. If yes, need the PO form filled this week.
[11:45] Evan: HR will supply the contractor list after this call — makes sense to lock down who gets access.
[12:05] Sofia: okay, next, endpoint protection — we have two potential vendors, Defender (MS) and CrowdStrike. Current telemetry suggests CrowdStrike has better detection but costs more. Michael, I'll send a short comparative spreadsheet.
[12:30] Michael: please include TCO over 3 years, not just seat price — manpower to manage, false positive overhead, etc.
[12:50] Priya: also include compatibility with our VPC/on-prem setups; some agents are flaky in certain environments.
[13:10] Sofia: noted. I'll add notes about on-prem agent quirks.
[13:30] Jamal: badge readers question again: do we want separate readers for secure zones or a single system with partitioned groups? The partitioned approach reduces hardware but increases config complexity.
[13:55] Priya: security prefers partitioned groups to allow emergency lockdowns per zone.
[14:15] Sofia: ok, we'll document that in the physical security plan.
[14:35] Michael: any other finance asks? If not I'll follow up via email with the PO template.
[14:50] Evan: HR has a small policy ask — confirm that contractor badge expiration is enforced automatically.
[15:05] Sofia: we'll set auto-expiry for badges tied to contractor end date in HRIS. Evan please ensure dates are accurate in the HRIS.
[15:30] Priya: one more SOC2 note — incident response tabletop scheduled next month, we should sync dates so evidence of the tabletop exists for the audit.
[15:50] Jamal: can facilities be on that tabletop for physical intrusion scenario?
[16:05] Priya: yes, please.
[16:25] Sofia: ok we'll block calendar for a 90-min tabletop in April — Sofia to propose dates.
[16:45] Michael: wrap-up: Michael will get preliminary budget numbers and invoice schedule, Priya will finish evidence map, Sofia runbook and restore drill costs, Jamal badge plan, Evan HR lists.
[17:10] Sofia: great thanks everyone. I'll send notes + runbook draft and schedule the follow-up. Meeting end.
